evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.87, FIRST panel and first horizontal arrow, labelled 'delta-r H'. SUBSTRATE: the p.201 text names it explicitly -- 'delta-hydrogen transfer is operative in the elimination of isobutene from exo-tert-butyladamantanone, which proceeds through a seven-membered transition state (Lightner and Wijekoon 1985, Equation 8.87); note that no other competitive hydrogen transfers are possible, because of the molecule's rigid geometry. The endo-isomer loses only C4H9.' The drawn cage is adamantan-2-one carrying a tert-butyl group on the ring carbon TWO bonds from the carbonyl carbon (one bold-wedge and one hashed-wedge methyl mark the exo configuration), i.e. exo-4-tert-butyladamantan-2-one, C14H22O, M+. m/z 206.1665. Atom maps: 1 = carbonyl O, 2 = C2 (carbonyl C), 4 = C3 (alpha, bridgehead), 5 = C4 (beta, bears the tert-butyl), 12 = the quaternary tert-butyl C (gamma), 13 = the delta methyl that donates the H, 20 = the migrating H (written [1H:20] so RDKit keeps it as a mapped atom). The transition-state ring O(1)-C(2)-C(4)-C(5)-C(12)-C(13)-H(20) contains SEVEN atoms, exactly as the text states. STEREOCHEMISTRY: the exo relative configuration drawn with the wedges is NOT encoded in the mapped SMILES (corpus convention); it is what makes this delta transfer geometrically possible, and its absence is why the endo isomer instead loses C4H9. (B) LOCALIZATION: the book prints '+.' directly on the carbonyl oxygen, so the precursor is written n-ionized at oxygen, [O+:1]=[C:2] (O with two bonds -> charge +1 and one odd electron); the product panel prints 'HO' with a '+' over the oxygen and a radical dot on the CH2, i.e. a DISTONIC ion whose charge sits on the three-coordinate protonated-carbonyl oxygen (closed shell there) and whose odd electron sits on the primary carbon C(13). ARCS: Book draws 1 arc -- a single-barbed FISHHOOK whose tail sits on the drawn H-CH2 bond and whose head (one barb only, verified at 22x magnification) points at the oxygen. Move <1> (one electron of the C(13)-H(20) bond delivered to the forming O-H bond) is that drawn arc; move <2> (the oxygen's own odd electron pairing into the same forming O-H bond) and move <3> (the implicit homolysis hook that leaves the odd electron on C(13) as the drawn .CH2) are required for electron balance but are NOT drawn on the page. NO m/z and NO percentage is printed for either the molecular ion or this intermediate, so both are detected=false.

Equation 8.87, SECOND panel and second horizontal arrow, labelled 'alpha'. The drawn intermediate carries the radical on the primary carbon C(13) ('.CH2') and the charge on the protonated carbonyl oxygen; alpha cleavage at that carbon radical breaks the C(5)-C(12) bond -- the bond between the adamantane ring carbon and the quaternary tert-butyl carbon -- forming the C(12)=C(13) double bond of isobutene and leaving the odd electron on the ring carbon C(5). The charged fragment is therefore the distonic ion 'protonated-carbonyl oxygen + ring carbon radical', C10H14O+., which the book writes simply as (M - C4H8)+., 100%. ARCS: Book draws 2 arcs, both single-barbed fishhooks -- one whose tail starts at the radical dot of .CH2 and whose head points onto the forming C(12)=C(13) bond, and one whose tail sits on the C(5)-C(12) bond (the near-vertical line from the quaternary carbon up to the ring) and whose head points onto the same forming C(12)=C(13) bond. Moves <1,2> are those two drawn arcs; move <3> (the second electron of the breaking C(5)-C(12) sigma bond dropping onto the ring carbon C(5) as a radical) is the implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance and is NOT drawn on the page -- the book indicates it only by writing the products. The '100%' printed to the right of (M - C4H8)+. is the only intensity on this scheme; the electron energy is not printed on the page, so the 70 eV EI value in ms_context is the chapter-default convention, not a page datum. m/z values (206.1665 for M+., 150.1039 for (M - C4H8)+., 56.0626 for the neutral isobutene) are curator-computed monoisotopic values; the book prints none of them.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.87 (chapter-8 keys stop at 8.14), so NO MOD rule is cross-linked. The two nearest generic encodings were checked against the instantiated substrate by RDKit substructure match and BOTH FAIL. (1) STEP 1: hTransition_saturated_4 ('H transition receptor site saturated rH §Y8', IMS_bookCover.py) '[H]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]5[C]6([H]7){=}[_A+.]8>>[C.]2[C]3[C]4[C]5[C]6([H]7){=}[_A+]8[H]1' is the right topology -- a delta-H transfer along a five-carbon chain to a doubly-bonded charged-radical heteroatom, i.e. the seven-membered transition state of Equation 8.87 -- but its left side demands an explicit hydrogen [H]7 on the sp2 carbon [C]6, which restricts it to ALDEHYDES. The carbonyl carbon of 4-tert-butyladamantan-2-one is a ring ketone carbon with no hydrogen, and the corresponding SMARTS [#1]-[#6]-[#6]-[#6]-[#6]-[#6](-[#1])=[O+] gives 0 matches on the precursor, while the same query with the sp2 hydrogen removed gives 24 matches (the delta path of 8.87 among them). The rule is a coverage gap for ketones, not a match. (2) STEP 2: hTransition_unsaturated_alpha '[C.]1[C]2[C]3[C]4{=}[_A+]5[H]6>>[C]1{=}[C]2.[C.]3[C]4{=}[_A+]5[H]6' cleaves the bond one carbon closer to the carbonyl than Equation 8.87 does: its chain is C.-C-C-C=O+ (0 matches on the distonic intermediate) whereas the 8.87 chain is C.-C-C-C-C=O+ (1 match). hTransition_saturated_4_alpha '[C.]1[C]2[C]3[C]4([H]5){=}[O+]7[C]8>>[C]1[C]2[C]3{-}1.[C]4([H]5){=}[O+.]7[C]8' is not an alpha cleavage at all -- its right side closes a three-membered carbocycle (a radical-site DISPLACEMENT, the Equation 4.37 pattern) and it too requires an aldehyde/ester-type [H]5 (or [C]8) on the sp2 carbon. Equation 8.87 is therefore UNMODELLED by the current MOD rule set in both of its steps.
